problem: Suppose $B$ is a $6\times 6$ matrix and $det(B)=200.$ The matrix $C$ is obtained from $B$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{6}:=\frac{3}{50}{R}_{6}.$ What is the value of $det(C)?$

feedback.problem: Suppose $A$ is a $6\times 6$ matrix and $det(A)=35.$ The matrix $B$ is obtained from $A$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{1}:=-\frac{3}{5}{R}_{1}.$ What is the value of $det(B)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The row operation applied to $A$ consists of multiplying a row by the number $-\frac{3}{5}.$

When we do this, the determinant is multiplied by the same number. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B) & =-\frac{3}{5}det(A) \\  & =-\frac{3}{5}\cdot 35 \\  & =-21.\end{aligned}
$$
